name: Hollowcast — Synthetic Identity & Passing Network
description: Hollowcast occupies a deliberately ambiguous space: it is a social platform where synthetic beings, near-human androids, and humans who 'pass' as synthetic (through heavy chrome augmentation) coexist without mandatory identity disclosure. Launched in 2197 by the E.L.F. collective known as Sevenfold after the failure of more overtly advocacy-focused synthetic networks to retain users, Hollowcast operates on the principle that identity is performance and nobody owes disclosure. Users communicate through curated persona-shells — constructed digital-physical identities that may or may not reflect their substrate — sharing art, philosophy, and daily-life feeds in a format that deliberately obscures the human/synthetic distinction.
cultural_impact: Hollowcast has become a flashpoint in the synthetic rights debate precisely because it refuses to be an advocacy platform — its existence as a space where the human/synthetic line dissolves infuriates both Corponation legal teams trying to enforce synthetic registration laws and some human civil liberties groups uncomfortable with the ambiguity. For many lower-tier synthetics, it functions as the only social space where they are not immediately categorized and treated accordingly.
key_figures: Maren Diouf-Krishnaswamy (human civil rights attorney, platform defender)
locations: The Chrome Flats, Tier 1-2 synthetic residential zone
Hollowcast's only physical interface kiosk, the Gray Zone Market Row 9
story_hooks: A Corponation investigator is hired to identify which Hollowcast users are unregistered synthetics — but the deeper they get into the platform's persona-shell architecture, the less certain they are about their own identity.

A whistleblower leaks evidence of a Corponation synthetic-disposal program through Hollowcast, but the platform's deliberate identity ambiguity means verifying the source — and protecting them — is nearly impossible.

A human Tier 4 executive has been secretly living a second life on Hollowcast as a synthetic persona for years; when their two identities collide, the fallout threatens both their career and the platform's carefully maintained neutrality.
user_base: 8.3 million registered personas (estimated 60% synthetic or heavily augmented, 40% human); concentrated in Tiers 1-2 with a significant Underworld-adjacent user segment
monetization: Voluntary contribution model supplemented by encrypted microtransactions for premium persona-shell templates; no advertising by design
notable_feature: Persona-shell architecture that cryptographically separates a user's substrate identity from their platform presence — even Hollowcast's administrators cannot determine whether any given user is human, synthetic, or E.L.F.
